first.rationale: With only one experiment slot, I'm prioritizing the onboarding completion decline (down 4% QoQ) using the two corroborating, clean-source memories (86, 31) showing durable activation/adoption lift from reducing signup/onboarding friction — this addresses both the onboarding and activation softness simultaneously without chasing the competitor's price war. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitive threat, but that memory explicitly flags a pooled-cohort readout from a mid-test redefinition, so its effect size is unreliable; racing to match aggressive entry pricing also risks attracting low-quality, low-retention SMB revenue that undermines the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. I'm spending verification on memory_73 to check whether the pooled-cohort issue changes the picture enough to reconsider, and on memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-shortening evidence is solid before committing this week's only slot to it. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are lower urgency given current metrics and are deferred, not abandoned.
